title: Beef Vindaloo
description: An authentic, fiery, melt-in-your-mouth beef curry that doesn't muck around.

ingredients.notes: Don't add too much all at once — you can't take it out once it's in.

method.instruction: Prepare 1 batch of [[vindaloopaste|Vindaloo Paste]] according to the recipe. Set aside.
Place beef in a large bowl. Add the vindaloo paste and toss to coat evenly. Cover and marinate at least 1 hour at room temperature, or refrigerate overnight for deeper flavour.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat. Add onions and sauté 2–3 minutes until soft. Add garlic and sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, and white vinegar. Cook 2–3 minutes until tomatoes break down.
Add marinated beef and sugar. Season with salt. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in hot water, bring to the boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour or until beef is tender and sauce has thickened.
If sauce is too thin, uncover and simmer for a further 5–10 minutes to reduce.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with steamed rice.

notes.title: Vinegar Substitute
notes.content: You can substitute white vinegar with apple cider vinegar, rice wine vinegar, or lemon juice for similar acidity and flavour.

notes.title: Overnight Marinade
notes.content: For the deepest flavour, marinate the beef overnight in the refrigerator. The vinegar and spices will tenderise the meat while infusing it with flavour.

notes.title: Paste Yield
notes.content: The vindaloo paste recipe yields approximately 80–100 g — exactly the right amount for 1 kg of beef. Use the full batch.
